questions.question: Explain why the land in the opening scenario stays at R500 000 in the books, and why accounting chooses this treatment even though the market value is R900 000.
questions.expected_answer: The historical cost principle requires assets to be recorded at their original, verifiable purchase price. The R500 000 is a fact supported by a source document, while the R900 000 is an opinion that can change; accounting prefers verifiable fact so that statements remain objective and trustworthy.

questions.question: Historical cost and prudence are often confused. In your own words, explain the difference and give one example of each.
questions.expected_answer: Historical cost is about recording assets at their original purchase price (e.g. land kept at R500 000 despite a higher market value). Prudence is about choosing the cautious figure when uncertainty exists — anticipating losses but never anticipating profits (e.g. writing off a doubtful debt or valuing damaged stock at the lower value).

questions.question: Describe the method you would use in an exam to identify which GAAP principle a scenario demonstrates. Apply it to: 'The owner's private car is not shown among the business's vehicles.'
questions.expected_answer: Underline the action and ask what the accountant is refusing or insisting on doing. Here the accountant refuses to mix the owner's personal property with the business's records, which is the business entity rule — the business and its owner are separate entities in the books.
